newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling edges up on dlr in seesaw trade.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling edges up on dlr in seesaw trade.

text.p: Dollar inflows from foreign investors helped firm the Kenyan shilling against the dollar on Friday, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 54.05 against the dollar from 54.31 on Thursday, while against the pound it was posted at a commercial mean of 88.12 from 89.52.
"Importers kept off the market which helped ease pressure on the shilling," one dealer said.
Investors, uncertain of the shilling's direction after a week of volatile trade, were driving the shilling up and down by speculating, dealers said.
"They didn't really know why the shilling moved the way it did, so they're coming in and going out," a dealer said.
The shilling was trading at 54.50/55.00 at mid-morning, dealers said.
The money market continued liquid. Overnight rates were quoted at 8 percent unchanged.
